doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Playing what you hear
summary: He still thinks hearing and playing what you hear is the greatest challenge.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Just recently, no I’m sorry, this is 1986, you said, “Playing what you hear is the greatest challenge.”

I still believe it. I mean because it’s very easy to get, I mean and I still do, we all do, it’s very easy for us to get wrapped up in like finger wiggling or knowing you know well like or just sort of going on automatic pilot. And you have to have a certain amount of that, that’s just like technique and vocabulary but it’s nice to be able to really, it’s nice when you can start to hear all of these things when you play that it comes out in a way that’s not so premeditated and natural. And that you hear it as you’re playing, you can sort of hear one phrase moving into another phrase and there’s a logic to it. I still think it’s the greatest challenge because I don’t do it all the time. I mean I try, you know, when I’m playing at my best I’m really hearing everything for most of what I play. But it’s not always going to be the case.
